 Mike Tomlin Expected To Be Top Coaching Candidate In 2027
 By Ely Allen |
 at November 15, 2026 8:26 pm 
 We’re two weeks into November, and there hasn’t been a single head coach firing 10 weeks into the season. The last time we had to wait until November for the first head coaching change was 2017, so we’re in an unusual position at this point in the season of not knowing what jobs will be open for 2027. Regardless of which teams will be searching, Mark Maske of Front Office Sports argues that NBC analyst Mike Tomlin will likely be a top candidate for any vacant positions.
 Tomlin, the former Steelers head coach of 19 years, has proven that he possesses more than one talent valuable to the NFL community. As a studio analyst for NBC’s Sunday Night Football , Tomlin has drawn rave reviews in his first few months on the job. He chose to step away from coaching altogether as he departed from Pittsburgh, unlike fellow longtime AFC North skipper John Harbaugh .
 Currently sitting atop the NFC East, Harbaugh’s Giants have proven to be the latest example of a franchise being rejuvenated by a veteran coaching addition. The Broncos, with head coach Sean Payton , are another example which actually draws quite a few parallels with Tomlin’s current situation. Payton chose to retire from coaching in the 2022 offseason. A year later, he accepted the head coaching position in Denver, and by the end of his third season, he had coached the team to its first division title and trip to the AFC Championship Game in 10 years.
 Such success stories make Tomlin an obvious person of interest in the soon-to-come hiring season, but there may end up being a few barriers for teams trying to add the 54-year-old to their staff. For starters, Maske reports that Tomlin is truly enjoying his time in television. While an NFL opportunity will bring with it quite a large contract, reports seem to indicate that Tomlin isn’t making chump change at NBC.
 The details of his contract have not been disclosed, but Maske implies that the deal is believed to be “lucrative by industry standards.” Now, the contract doesn’t serve as a barrier itself; the deal does keep Tomlin from leaving NBC for another network, but it permits him to depart for a coaching job, if he so chooses.
 The other potential speed bump to hiring Tomlin is that the Steelers likely still hold his coaching rights. When he retired, Tomlin had just concluded the first year of a three-year extension. This year would’ve been the second, and the contract could’ve extended through the 2027 season with the exercising of a team option. It’s currently not known if Tomlin’s team option was exercised before his resignation, but if he were to return to the NFL to coach, he would likely be subject to at least one year, if not two, of team control.
 This is one area in which Tomlin’s situation parallels that of Payton’s before he joined the Broncos. Payton became the latest in a line of storied head coaches — Bill Parcells , Bill Belichick , Jon Gruden , and Herm Edwards , to name a few — to be traded between organizations. Depending on how Tomlin’s contract was processed upon his departure, any team that decides to hire him may need to part with some draft capital in order to do so.
 While no changes in coaching leadership have come quite yet this NFL season, franchises with rumored hot seats in Los Angeles (Chargers), Washington, New York (Jets), and Indianapolis may be doing their homework on Tomlin as a potential candidate. It’s not a sure thing that he’ll be available, though, as he may not choose to return to coaching, and the Steelers may end up with an asking price that some won’t be able to afford.
 For a hint at where his mind may be on the matter, ESPN’s Brooke Pryor provided his response to a question on the topic in a recent NBC Sports conference call.  “Haven’t given one iota of thought about coaching,” Tomlin told those on the call.  “I’m sure that’ll come up in the not so distant future, but I’ll cross that bridge when I get to it.”
